analysis:
The PR removes the retained console-ui lane from CI and drops the console output of the component-changes workflow. It also edits AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md to say the web console now lives in darkbloom-platform. No provider runtime code changes: the WebSocket protocol (TB-002), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), encryption, prefix cache (T-041), fan helper (TB-010) and add-on hold (TB-012) are not touched, so no threat-model assumption is invalidated.

ci.yml: the route lanes no longer include lint-console, and the lint-console job is deleted (base 637-658). The remaining provider jobs keep SHA-pinned actions, `permissions: contents read` and `persist-credentials: false` on the classifier checkout. The provider-test-gate only requires the provider lanes, so removing the console job does not weaken a provider gate. No new secrets, triggers or permissions were added.

component-changes.yml: the console output was removed from both the workflow_call outputs and the job outputs, and ci.yml no longer references needs.changes.outputs.console. This is consistent in the supplied files. The unseen scripts/ci-component-paths.py may still emit a console output, and scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py, scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py and docs-check may still expect console-ui paths or the lint-console lane. That would be a CI breakage or drift issue, not a security regression. The supplied changes are limited to the workflow and doc files, so these scripts were not examined.

Docs: the AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md edits are ownership and navigation text only. The retained coordinator/tests/protocol/testdata fixtures are still described as shared protocol fixtures, not a coordinator implementation. One open question: whether the console-ui directory, its hosting configuration or Makefile ui targets are removed elsewhere in the PR. If console-ui remains, it would no longer be linted or tested by CI. That is outside the supplied units.
